description.value: The study examined whether the first behavioral symptom of bvFTD, apathy or disinhibition, is associated with later neuropsychological and neuroanatomical profiles and whether these features distinguish patient subgroups.

spans.text: Here, we evaluated the neuropsychological and neuroanatomical correlates (measured at an average of 3 years after the report of the first symptom) in a group of controls and two groups of bvFTD patients (debuting with apathy or disinhibition).

design.value: Cross-sectional comparison of healthy controls and two bvFTD patient groups defined retrospectively by their first symptom, with neuropsychological assessment, structural MRI voxel-based morphometry, brain-behavior correlations, and multivariate classification analyses.

spans.text: We evaluated the neuropsychological, clinical, and neuroanatomical (3T structural images) correlates in a group of healthy controls (n = 30) and two groups of bvFTD patients (presented with apathy [AbvFTD, n = 18] or disinhibition [DbvFTD, n = 16]). To differentiate groups according to first symptoms, we used multivariate analyses.

description.value: VBM preprocessing included normalization to stereotaxic space using DARTEL, segmentation into WM, GM and non-brain voxels, modulation with Jacobian determinants, and smoothing with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

spans.text: The T1-weighted images were normalized to the same stereotaxic space generated from the complete data set using the DARTEL algorithm that significantly reduces the imprecision of inter-subject registration. Then, the images were segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels (CSF, skull). Subsequently, all images were modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants. Finally, images were smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum for statistical analyses.

steps.value: Images were inspected for artifacts; normalized with DARTEL; segmented into WM, GM and non-brain voxels; modulated with Jacobian determinants; smoothed with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

spans.text: Each image was inspected for artifacts. All imaging analysis processes were conducted as described in the VBM pipeline (http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/ john/misc/VBM) and are briefly summarized as follows. The T1-weighted images were normalized to the same stereotaxic space generated from the complete data set using the DARTEL algorithm that significantly reduces the imprecision of inter-subject registration. Then, the images were segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels (CSF, skull). Subsequently, all images were modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants. Finally, images were smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum for statistical analyses.
Neuroanatomical correlates were analyzed using VBM method.
